clue.text: Ring round record — the lone discrepancy

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the short record, enclosing it
discrepancy suggests the letters of the and lone are out of order and must be rearranged

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A loner phones round about a recording that doesn't match the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a circle, but it is the verb to call; 'discrepancy' rearranges THE LONE into TELHONE before 'round' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to call them on the phone, a verb sense.

clue.text: Brick used in bridge

definitions.meaning: a brick is a good, reliable fellow
in the card game bridge, a card of the leading suit that beats others

explanation.surface: A building brick used in constructing a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A good sort is a dependable friend; in card games a winning suit card beats the rest.

clue.text: The pound is to a certain extent flexible

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
some means to some degree

explanation.surface: Sterling's value is somewhat adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and lithe describes a body that bends easily.

clue.text: Shanghai newspapermen?

definitions.meaning: to shanghai is to force someone into service as a sailor
journalists are the press, and a group of them a gang

explanation.surface: Journalists based in a Chinese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing men into naval service was impressment; reporters collectively are a press crew.

clue.text: Jack, in total, is convalescent

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the phrase for total

parts.note: out-and-out means utter, total
a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is, all told, recovering from illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a traditional name for a sailor; the able seaman's AB splits the total phrase after its AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering who is up and moving around again after illness.

clue.text: Finish two points behind, finally

parts.note: E for east is one compass point
N for north is the second compass point

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word behind

explanation.surface: A team ends the season two points adrift.
explanation.definitionFit: The close or conclusion of something.

clue.text: Flick one in turn

indicators.note: in puts the numeral for one inside the word for a turn

parts.note: a turn in a game is a move
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone flicks a counter on their turn in a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A flick is informal for a film shown at the cinema.

clue.text: Climb a hill

definitions.meaning: a mountain or hill, as in a name like ... Everest

explanation.surface: An instruction to go up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go up; a peak or eminence is a hill.

clue.text: He behaves badly with football club at home

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, called Villa
in means at home

explanation.surface: A footballer misbehaves at his club's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club, always called Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or wrongdoer is a person who acts wickedly.

clue.text: Always 5. the French, and cunning

parts.note: 5 down means finish, a word meaning the close
les is French for the (plural)
sly means cunning

explanation.surface: A list of three qualities for someone permanently French and crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: Without stopping, forever and continually.

clue.text: "Still to be cleaned" 'itler's gang cried

parts.note: Hitler's gang, the Huns, with the H dropped as the clue drops it from Hitler, gives 'UNS
to have cried is to have wept

explanation.surface: A quoted notice about an uncleaned room, then the Nazis bursting into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''itler' signals that the Huns (old slang for Germans) also lose their H, giving 'UNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Floors not yet swept with a broom are still to be cleaned.

clue.text: Ran in tandem?

parts.note: tandem suggests a two-seater bicycle, but the reading is that running as a pair means moving at twice the pace, or folding into two

explanation.surface: Two cyclists riding a bicycle built for two.
explanation.definitionFit: To go at double pace is to run, and in tandem things come twice over, so the clue hints at a two-fold sense.

clue.text: Smug clergyman thrown out by prior

indicators.note: thrown out by says the clergyman's letters are expelled from the word for prior

parts.note: prior means earlier, previous
REV is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied vicar is ejected from the priory by its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctimonious, holier-than-thou person can seem smug about their virtue.

clue.text: Dream of the margin of error

indicators.note: of error says the letters of the margin are mistakenly arranged and must be put right

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fantasises about the statistical margin of error.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying dream during sleep is a bad dream.

clue.text: Second flight doesn't finish in disaster for these birds

indicators.note: in disaster says the letters are in a mess and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: doesn't finish says the word flight loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An airline's second flight crashes before landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't finish' cuts FLIGHT to FLIGH; 'in disaster' rearranges SECOND FLIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Small finches with gold wing bars are a kind of songbird.

clue.text: Hurry up and say hello

indicators.note: say means the word for hello is spoken, giving the sound of the entry

parts.note: hi is an informal hello

explanation.surface: Someone told to rush and greet a visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an archaic verb meaning to hasten or go quickly.

clue.text: U Vith?

definitions.meaning: U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U usage
the VIth is the sixth form, the top class at a British school

explanation.surface: A cryptic shorthand of a letter and a school form.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth form is the final years of a British secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-crust or posh is upper class; the senior school form is a top class.

clue.text: Where the ardent sports fan can be seen, in any case

definitions.text: Where the ardent sports fan can be seen
definitions.meaning: a keen fan turns up at every fixture or competition
a phrase meaning whatever happens, anyway

explanation.surface: A keen supporter is found everywhere, anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the phrase places the fan at every competition; idiomatically it means regardless.

clue.text: Pests gobble up fuel that's coloured

indicators.note: gobble says the pests swallow the fuel, taking it inside

parts.note: vermin are pests

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the fuel is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Rats eat through fuel that has been dyed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses, giving LIO; 'gobble' then has the pests swallow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant scarlet red, so tinted bright red.

clue.text: To forgo gain is unusual, exceeding normal limits

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of to forgo gain are in an odd order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Turning down profit is rare and seen as excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for overstepping the mark or doing more than is acceptable.

clue.text: It'll be longer in hospital, I anticipate

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words hospital, I anticipate

explanation.surface: A patient expects a longer hospital stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a short form of the word (as in gin and It, Italian vermouth), so the longer form is the full word.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation It stands for the full nationality word, which is the longer form.

clue.text: To begin with, it's cold, yes, very cold

indicators.note: To begin with says take the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that, at first, it really is freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Freezing weather or water is described as frosty, glacial.

clue.text: Reluctance to move — but I retain some movement

indicators.note: some movement says the letters of retain are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy person admits to keeping some motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is only a link; 'some movement' rearranges RETAIN into NERTIA, placed after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: The tendency of a body to stay at rest, or a lack of energy.

clue.text: One making false claims about birth, retracted after 27

parts.note: 27 across is a word meaning to scorch, the same as char

indicators.note: retracted says the word for relating to birth is drawn back, read in reverse

parts.note: natal means concerning birth

explanation.surface: Someone lying about their origins withdraws the story later.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 27 across, whose definition word supplies CHAR; 'retracted' turns NATAL into LATAN, and 'after' places it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud or quack pretends to skills or knowledge they lack.

clue.text: Go away for a holiday

definitions.meaning: time off work, as soldiers get

explanation.surface: Someone departs on a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away; time off granted is a holiday period.

clue.text: I provide hands in perfect condition

parts.note: to deal is to give out hands of cards

explanation.surface: A carer says they supply helpers in excellent shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion of flawlessness is a standard of excellence one aims at.

clue.text: Deposit put up

definitions.meaning: to deposit something, as in a formal complaint
to put up a guest, to house them

explanation.surface: A notice saying that a deposit has been posted.
explanation.definitionFit: To place formally, as a complaint, is to deposit it; to house guests is to put them up.

clue.text: Maid in a considerable amount of trouble

parts.note: big means large in amount
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A housemaid is in a great deal of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid, from a servant character in a seventeenth-century play.

clue.text: Cover from one pound to five hundred

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Prices ranging from a single pound to five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A top or cap that closes a container.

clue.text: Did some raising, having first removed the weeds outside

indicators.note: outside puts the word for weeding around the abbreviation for first

parts.note: to hoe is to remove weeds with a garden tool
1st is first, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A gardener lifted something after weeding the area outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST, with the 1 read as I, goes inside HOED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting with a rope or pulley is raising something up.

clue.text: Char has son by Dean

parts.note: William Inge was Dean of St Paul's, known as the Gloomy Dean

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady has a child by a cathedral dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like a cleaning lady (British slang), but it means scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch the surface lightly is to burn it a little.

clue.text: Stop fighting and give up the ring

definitions.meaning: to break off an engagement to marry, read as dis- plus a word for betrothal

explanation.surface: A boxer quits the bout and leaves the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing forces is disengaging; ending a betrothal is undoing an engagement.
